etymologies.etymologyHTML: From heat +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: A device that produces and radiates heat, typically to raise the temperature of a room or building.
A person who heats something, for example in metalworking.
(baseball, slang) A fastball, especially one thrown at high velocity.
(historical) A medieval European shield having a rounded triangle shape like a clothes iron.

quote.citation: 1998, John Clements, Medieval Swordsmanship: Illustrated Methods and Techniques:
quote.text: It can be assumed that as the earlier kite shield transformed into the heater shape, there must have been versions in between the two styles. Indeed, in artwork of the Medieval period, shields are rarely present after 1450 and even then are quite small. The development of flattop heaters from larger kite shields is likely the result of increased fighting on horseback and the use of improved armor.

definitions.definition: (horse racing) A dead heat; a race in which two or more competitors reach the finish line simultaneously.
